subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should Azure Foundry / Azure OpenAI Realtime Talk be supported as an OpenAI provider gateway-relay mode, a separate azure-openai provider alias, or deferred until Entra/SecretRef/live-proof requirements are settled?
rationale: The permanent choice affects provider identity, config shape, SecretRef and Entra handling, browser credential boundaries, diagnostics, docs, and live validation, so automation cannot safely pick the product/API contract.

options.title: Use OpenAI gateway-relay mode
options.body: Keep provider id openai, require gateway-relay for Azure realtime config, and add explicit Azure endpoint/deployment/auth validation and docs.

options.title: Add azure-openai alias
options.body: Expose Azure as a distinct provider identity while mapping to OpenAI-compatible realtime internals, accepting extra provider-routing and docs compatibility work.

options.title: Defer until live quota exists
options.body: Leave the feature open but avoid implementation until maintainers can deploy a current Azure Realtime model and verify the endpoint/auth behavior.

recommendation.title: Use OpenAI gateway-relay mode
recommendation.body: Keep provider id openai, require gateway-relay for Azure realtime config, and add explicit Azure endpoint/deployment/auth validation and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They already performed the Azure live availability check, and the next step is primarily a maintainer product/proof decision rather than a narrow code patch.
